## 13. Architex platform transaction fee and escrow monetisation

Architex monetises project cash flow by charging a transparent platform transaction/service fee of approximately 1% on transactions processed through the platform. This must be disclosed in proposals, invoices, escrow funding requests, payment confirmations and ledger records.
- Total Architex service cost: 1.00% of the chargeable transaction base
- Client / payer contribution: 0.50% added on top of the professional fee or construction bill
- Professional / contractor / payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the amount released to the payee
- Architex receives both halves through the escrow/payment gateway flow
Example on a R100,000 professional fee or construction bill, excluding VAT and excluding statutory disbursements unless deliberately included:
- Client-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
- Client funds into escrow before VAT/payment-gateway effects: R100,500.00
- Payee-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
Every proposal and bill generated through Architex must include a visible line item such as:

"Architex platform transaction/service fee: 1.00% total, shared equally between payer and payee. Client contribution: 0.50% added to this payment. Payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the release amount. Processed through Architex escrow/payment gateway."
- Fee/bill before Architex transaction service fee
- VAT treatment and payment-gateway fees separately, pending tax/accounting confirmation
- Contractor construction bills / certified payment amounts
- Supplier bills where paid through Architex marketplace/escrow
- Payment gateway processing fees if separately charged
For each accepted proposal/payment stage, Architex should create a split settlement schedule:
1. Client funds gross amount into escrow: chargeableBase + clientPlatformFee + other included charges
2. Escrow records the full held amount
3. On milestone release, Architex deducts payeePlatformFee from payee gross release
5. Architex platform account receives clientPlatformFee + payeePlatformFee
6. Ledger records separate entries for escrow deposit, client platform fee, payee platform fee, payee release, refunds/reversals and gateway fees
The current Architex repo already contains relevant foundations:
- `src/services/feeEstimatorService.ts` includes fee-estimator settings and currently has `platformFeePercent` defaulted to 5. This should be replaced or superseded by the 1% split transaction model.
- `src/services/paymentService.ts` contains `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENTAGE = 0.05` and escrow/milestone payment logic. This should become a structured split-fee calculation, not a flat 5% added fee.

- `src/services/financialLedgerService.ts` already records ledger entries and recognises `platform_fee`. It should be extended to distinguish `platform_fee_client_share` and `platform_fee_payee_share`.

- `src/types.ts` already includes payments, escrow, invoices, ledger, project lifecycle, tenders and contractor-facing role types. The proposal builder can extend these rather than starting from scratch.

- Add ledger entries for both sides of the fee.

## 3. Product principle: convenient agentic tool access
Do not make users hunt through a giant tools menu. Architex should expose tools through four convenient surfaces:
- A persistent toolbox in each dashboard, filtered by role and project stage.
- Tools shown inside the current project phase: brief, appointment, design, council, tender, construction, closeout.

- Drawings and models should be first-class data sources, not just uploaded files. Agents must be able to read PDFs, scanned/image drawings, DWG/DXF, IFC/BIM exports, Revit-derived schedules, Excel schedules and marked-up site photos where technically possible.

- Extracted data should include rooms, areas, levels, walls, openings, windows, doors, stairs, roof geometry, fire routes, parking counts, site coverage, boundary/building lines, fixtures, finishes, schedules, notes and title-block revision metadata.

## 3. Product principle: convenient agentic tool access
Do not make users hunt through a giant tools menu. Architex should expose tools through four convenient surfaces:
- A persistent toolbox in each dashboard, filtered by role and project stage.
- Tools shown inside the current project phase: brief, appointment, design, council, tender, construction, closeout.
- Agent sees a message, upload, drawing revision, site log, tender package or payment claim and suggests the next tool.
- Every project object has tool actions: drawing → compare/revise/RFI; tender line → rate build-up/RFQ; site log → daywork/claim; invoice → payment/escrow/reconciliation.

- Drawings and models should be first-class data sources, not just uploaded files. Agents must be able to read PDFs, scanned/image drawings, DWG/DXF, IFC/BIM exports, Revit-derived schedules, Excel schedules and marked-up site photos where technically possible.

- Extracted data should include rooms, areas, levels, walls, openings, windows, doors, stairs, roof geometry, fire routes, parking counts, site coverage, boundary/building lines, fixtures, finishes, schedules, notes and title-block revision metadata.
- The output must always state confidence, source drawing revision, assumptions and items needing professional/manual verification.

- The same extracted project information should be reusable through the commercial workflow: drawing takeoff → BoM → BoQ → contractor/subcontractor/QS review → editable quotes → programme activities → cashflow/drawdown schedule → payment valuations and escrow release milestones.
- Quantities should be pre-populated but never silently final. Contractors, subcontractors and QSs must be able to edit, override, qualify, exclude and version their review.

if (/xa|energy|glazing|fenestration|u-value|shgc|insulation|r-value/.test(text)) { push('Use the XA calculator set and keep the output as compliance support pending competent-person review.', ['xa_fenestration_quick_check', 'xa_rvalue_check']); } if (/storm|runoff|drain|catchment|rain|attenuation/.test(text)) { push('Use stormwater calculators and confirm municipal rainfall/intensity assumptions.', ['rational_method_runoff']); } if (/concrete|pour|slab|footing|cube|ready.?mix/.test(text)) { push('Use contractor concrete quantity/order calculator and export to supplier RFQ or site log.', ['concrete_order']); } if (/brick|block|masonry|wall/.test(text)) { push('Use masonry calculator for order quantities and subcontractor package quantities.', ['brick_blockwork']); } if (/rate|tender|bid|boq|price|quote|variation/.test(text)) { push('Use tender rate build-up calculator and lock assumptions when submitting bid/variation.', ['tender_rate_buildup']); } if (/labour|crew|productivity|duration|programme|program/.test(text)) { push('Use labour/productivity calculator and compare against site log actuals.', ['labour_productivity']); }

if (!recommendations.length) { recommendations.push({ agentId: 'toolbox_router_agent', message: 'No exact calculator detected. Show the role-specific toolbox and ask for dimensions, trade, source drawing and intended export target.', severity: 'info', suggestedCalculatorIds: available.slice(0, 5).map((item) => item.id), }); }

if (run.professionalSignoffRequired) { notes.push({ agentId: 'compliance_caution_agent', message: 'This result requires competent professional review/sign-off before being used for statutory, engineering or final design purposes.', severity: 'warning', suggestedExportTargets: ['rfi', 'bim_coordination_comment', 'compliance_report'], }); } if (run.riskStatus === 'fail') { notes.push({ agentId: 'input_completion_agent', message: 'Calculator returned a fail/risk result. Architex should provide role-specific calculators that help professionals structure, test, and issue fee proposals for projects. The calculators should not pretend to set fixed prices. They should convert recognised South African guideline frameworks into transparent proposal tools.
The platform should support two related use cases:
- Helps a client understand likely professional and statutory costs before appointing a team.

## 13. Architex platform transaction fee and escrow monetisation

Architex monetises project cash flow by charging a transparent platform transaction/service fee of approximately 1% on transactions processed through the platform. This must be disclosed in proposals, invoices, escrow funding requests, payment confirmations and ledger records.
- Total Architex service cost: 1.00% of the chargeable transaction base
- Client / payer contribution: 0.50% added on top of the professional fee or construction bill
- Professional / contractor / payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the amount released to the payee
- Architex receives both halves through the escrow/payment gateway flow
Example on a R100,000 professional fee or construction bill, excluding VAT and excluding statutory disbursements unless deliberately included:
- Client-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
- Client funds into escrow before VAT/payment-gateway effects: R100,500.00
- Payee-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
Every proposal and bill generated through Architex must include a visible line item such as:

"Architex platform transaction/service fee: 1.00% total, shared equally between payer and payee. Client contribution: 0.50% added to this payment. Payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the release amount. Processed through Architex escrow/payment gateway."
- Fee/bill before Architex transaction service fee
- VAT treatment and payment-gateway fees separately, pending tax/accounting confirmation
- Contractor construction bills / certified payment amounts
- Supplier bills where paid through Architex marketplace/escrow
- Payment gateway processing fees if separately charged
For each accepted proposal/payment stage, Architex should create a split settlement schedule:
1. Client funds gross amount into escrow: chargeableBase + clientPlatformFee + other included charges
2. Escrow records the full held amount
3. On milestone release, Architex deducts payeePlatformFee from payee gross release
5. Architex platform account receives clientPlatformFee + payeePlatformFee
6. Ledger records separate entries for escrow deposit, client platform fee, payee platform fee, payee release, refunds/reversals and gateway fees

- `src/services/paymentService.ts` contains `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENTAGE = 0.05` and escrow/milestone payment logic. This should become a structured split-fee calculation, not a flat 5% added fee.

- `src/services/financialLedgerService.ts` already records ledger entries and recognises `platform_fee`. It should be extended to distinguish `platform_fee_client_share` and `platform_fee_payee_share`.

- `src/types.ts` already includes payments, escrow, invoices, ledger, project lifecycle, tenders and contractor-facing role types. The proposal builder can extend these rather than starting from scratch.

- Require explicit user visibility before payment: no hidden platform-fee deduction.

The proposal builder should be supported by an agentic workflow layer. The agents do not move money autonomously; they prepare, check, remind, reconcile and route approvals while humans/payment providers execute controlled actions.

# Architex South African Professional Fee Calculator Toolbox
Version: 0.1 draft Prepared for: Architex Context: South African built-environment professional services, proposal preparation, discipline toolboxes, project soft-cost estimation

Architex should provide role-specific calculators that help professionals structure, test, and issue fee proposals for projects. The calculators should not pretend to set fixed prices. They should convert recognised South African guideline frameworks into transparent proposal tools.
The platform should support two related use cases:
- Helps a client understand likely professional and statutory costs before appointing a team.
- Output is an indicative range, not a quote.
- Helps each professional prepare a fee proposal using their council/industry guideline, scope stages, complexity and disbursement assumptions.
- Output can flow into an Architex proposal/appointment pack.
- Whether the guideline is mandatory, recommended, or indicative
- Whether VAT is included or excluded
- Project value used for fee purposes
- Optional professional discount percentage, with reason and approval record
- Audit log of inputs, outputs, source version, discount, and user edits

"This calculator provides an indicative fee based on selected South African professional guideline sources and user inputs. The professional remains responsible for confirming scope, complexity, exclusions, disbursements, VAT, statutory fees and professional obligations before issuing a proposal."

## 13. Architex platform transaction fee and escrow monetisation

Architex monetises project cash flow by charging a transparent platform transaction/service fee of approximately 1% on transactions processed through the platform. This must be disclosed in proposals, invoices, escrow funding requests, payment confirmations and ledger records.
- Total Architex service cost: 1.00% of the chargeable transaction base
- Client / payer contribution: 0.50% added on top of the professional fee or construction bill
- Professional / contractor / payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the amount released to the payee
- Architex receives both halves through the escrow/payment gateway flow
Example on a R100,000 professional fee or construction bill, excluding VAT and excluding statutory disbursements unless deliberately included:
- Client-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
- Client funds into escrow before VAT/payment-gateway effects: R100,500.00
- Payee-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
Every proposal and bill generated through Architex must include a visible line item such as:

"Architex platform transaction/service fee: 1.00% total, shared equally between payer and payee. Client contribution: 0.50% added to this payment. Payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the release amount. Processed through Architex escrow/payment gateway."
- Fee/bill before Architex transaction service fee
- VAT treatment and payment-gateway fees separately, pending tax/accounting confirmation
- Contractor construction bills / certified payment amounts
- Supplier bills where paid through Architex marketplace/escrow
- Payment gateway processing fees if separately charged
For each accepted proposal/payment stage, Architex should create a split settlement schedule:
1. Client funds gross amount into escrow: chargeableBase + clientPlatformFee + other included charges
2. Escrow records the full held amount
3. On milestone release, Architex deducts payeePlatformFee from payee gross release
5. Architex platform account receives clientPlatformFee + payeePlatformFee
6. Ledger records separate entries for escrow deposit, client platform fee, payee platform fee, payee release, refunds/reversals and gateway fees

- `src/services/feeEstimatorService.ts` includes fee-estimator settings and currently has `platformFeePercent` defaulted to 5. This should be replaced or superseded by the 1% split transaction model.
- `src/services/paymentService.ts` contains `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENTAGE = 0.05` and escrow/milestone payment logic. This should become a structured split-fee calculation, not a flat 5% added fee.

- `src/services/financialLedgerService.ts` already records ledger entries and recognises `platform_fee`. It should be extended to distinguish `platform_fee_client_share` and `platform_fee_payee_share`.

- `src/types.ts` already includes payments, escrow, invoices, ledger, project lifecycle, tenders and contractor-facing role types. The proposal builder can extend these rather than starting from scratch.

- Add line-item support for client platform fee and payee platform fee.
- Add ledger entries for both sides of the fee.
- Lock the transaction-fee version into each issued proposal/invoice.
- Make the 1% / 0.5% / 0.5% values admin-configurable, but default to Architex’s current commercial model.
- Require explicit user visibility before payment: no hidden platform-fee deduction.

The proposal builder should be supported by an agentic workflow layer. The agents do not move money autonomously; they prepare, check, remind, reconcile and route approvals while humans/payment providers execute controlled actions.

This pack consolidates the next major Architex product expansion after the already-developed messaging, navigation, toolsets, calculators, CPD platform and agent orchestration packs.
It is prepared for Leor's review before anything is issued to Greg and Amy.
Architex should become the trusted project memory, workflow engine, commercial record and professional coordination layer for the South African built environment.

The platform should not simply be a set of helpful tools. It should become the operating system that links every message, document, professional decision, calculation, payment, quote, CPD record, instruction, snag, RFI and agent recommendation to a structured project lifecycle.
## Core missing foundation: Project Lifecycle Engine
The most important missing product layer is a central Project Lifecycle Engine.
This engine should define the project journey from:
Every module should plug into this lifecycle so Architex always knows:
- what stage the project is in
- what the project agent should recommend next
## Product modules included in this expansion pack
This pack covers the following modules:
Every new feature must produce or consume structured project records. A document, message, quote, payment, site diary, snag, instruction, CPD reminder or agent action must be linkable to:
The expansion must remain grounded in South African practice:
- SACAP, ECSA, SACQSP, SACPLAN, SACLAP, SACPCMP and SAGC professional contexts where relevant
- payment, escrow and VAT logic suitable for South African transactions
- construction phase documentation familiar to local professionals and contractors
Every project should have a live Project Passport: a permanent structured record of the project/building.
This turns Architex into the long-term memory of the project.
Uploaded drawings should not be dead files. Architex should extract title-block data, revisions, rooms, areas, schedules, fire routes, parking, compliance flags and submission-readiness issues.

Architex can create a high-value marketplace by supporting freelancers and candidate professionals, while routing outputs to registered professionals for review/sign-off where legally/professionally required.
Finance should be linked to deliverables, approvals, payment certificates and project milestones. This creates trust and a platform transaction-fee opportunity.

Agents should detect gaps before they become problems, such as missing appointment letters, stale RFIs, expired insurance, issue of drawings without revision notes, incomplete submission packs and payment claims without evidence.

This expansion does affect the earlier navigation framework. The impact is controlled: do not add every new module as a sidebar item. Project Passport, Lifecycle Engine, Risk Engine, Municipal Readiness, Tender/Procurement, Site Execution and Closeout should live inside Projects, Command Centre, Inbox or Admin surfaces rather than becoming separate sidebar entries.

ARCHITEX PROJECT COMMUNICATION ENGINE — FIRST ISSUE BRIEF V4 For: Greg, Amy and Architex product/development team Prepared from Leor/Hymie product direction
ISSUE TITLE Build the Architex Project Communication Engine: mobile-first chat applet + desktop Project Message Centre, sharing one project communication backend.
STRATEGIC DECISION Do not build a separate native desktop chat application at this stage. Build one communication system in the Architex PWA and expose it through two responsive interfaces:
A WhatsApp-familiar, phone-first applet/PWA surface for fast project communication, capture, uploads, voice notes, approvals, RFIs, instructions and site/design/planning records.
A richer view inside the existing Architex web app/project workspace for reviewing, searching, filtering, assigning, converting, linking and administering the same communication record.
The single backend layer that stores messages, files, structured captures, actions, AI context, audit history and project memory.
PRODUCT LINE Chat on the phone. Control centre on desktop. Structured project memory in Architex.

WHY THIS MATTERS Building projects currently fall back to WhatsApp because it is quick, familiar and convenient. Architex should not fight that behaviour. It should absorb the convenience of chat while correcting the weakness of ordinary group chats: lost decisions, scattered files, unclear approvals, missing audit trails, buried instructions and unstructured project memory.

The front-facing chat applet is therefore not a mini version of the whole Architex platform. It is the easiest doorway into Architex. For many clients, contractors and site users, this may be the main interface they use daily. For architects, project managers and administrators, the same communication must become structured project intelligence inside the full desktop workspace.
CURRENT ARCHITEX ARCHITECTURE FIT This issue should be built to suit the current Architex PWA architecture:
- Tailwind CSS v4 via @tailwindcss/vite; no tailwind.config file.
- Firebase Auth + Firestore for users, projects, messages and realtime subscriptions.
- Vercel Blob for file storage, not Firebase Storage.
- Existing Message and Conversation types in src/types.ts.
- Existing project lifecycle model: ProjectStage = intake, scoping, appointment, coordination, compliance, tender, delivery, payments, closeout.
- Existing project lifecycle services and construction/tender/council/closeout services should be used rather than duplicated.
- Existing LLM route /api/review and Gemini/OpenAI-compatible proxy should be reused or extended for communication AI actions.
IMPORTANT PRODUCT CORRECTION The phase selector is not enough. The app must be phase-aware in function, not just in label. The selected project phase/stage must dynamically change:
- Which Architex service receives structured outputs.
ARCHITEX PHASE MAPPING Use the existing ProjectStage model as the primary integration layer:
- Client enquiry, initial need, property information, contact details, budget range, project intent.
- Briefing, feasibility, constraints, site information, zoning/town-planning flags, concept direction.
- Architect appointment, fee proposal, professional team setup, access/permissions.
- Design coordination, consultant queries, design decisions, markups, drawing coordination.
- SANS/NBR checks, municipal submission preparation, council comments, missing signatures, energy/fire/accessibility issues.
- Tender package, contractor queries, clarifications, addenda, exclusions, alternatives, bid comparison.

- Construction/site functionality. This must retain rich site-heavy capability: site photos, site visit mode, RFI, instruction, variation, snag/defect, safety, progress, delivery/material, inspection and time/cost impact.
- Payment milestones, escrow, invoice queries, payment approvals, variation cost implications.
- Snag closeout, certificates, warranties, as-built docs, final account, occupation/maintenance documents.
PROJECT SWITCHER REQUIREMENT The applet must include a clear project dropdown/switcher at the top of the mobile interface and equivalent project context controls on desktop.
- The user selects the active project before communicating or capturing records.
- Changing project updates the message thread, capture context, actions, files, AI prompts and project pulse.
- The selected project must be visible at all times to prevent messages/photos being filed to the wrong project.
- The system should support users with multiple concurrent projects.
- The project selector should use the existing Architex job/project permissions so users only see projects they are authorised to access.
REQUIRED FUNCTIONALITY — MOBILE PROJECT CHAT APPLET The mobile interface must feel like project chat first.

- Project switcher/dropdown to select between different active projects. This is essential because users may be working across multiple jobs and must not have to leave the chat surface to change project context.
- Phase/stage selector or visible current stage indicator.
- AI tab with visible heading: “Suggested prompts”.
- Files/Records tab or lightweight record drawer.
- Record/send voice note, with later transcription support.
- Convert a message into an action/RFI/instruction/approval/etc.
- Show next actions relevant to the selected phase.
- Show AI suggested prompts relevant to the selected phase.
- Keep the composer simple and familiar.
REQUIRED FUNCTIONALITY — DESKTOP MESSAGE CENTRE The desktop interface must not be a separate desktop chat application. It should be an Architex web-app module inside the project workspace.
- Search and filters by phase, person, capture type, action status, attachment type and date.
- Split view: conversation on the left, structured record/action detail on the right.
- Link message to drawings, files, submission items, tender package, RFI, site log, invoice, closeout record, etc.
- Project pulse: open actions, overdue items, decisions needed, pending approvals, AI alerts.
The mobile and desktop UIs must read/write to the same Firestore collections and file records.
DATA MODEL EXTENSIONS Extend the current Message model without breaking existing messages.
- projectId?: string, while retaining jobId for backward compatibility.
- location?: { lat: number; lng: number; label?: string }.
AI TAB REQUIREMENT The AI tab must include this visible heading and description:
Suggested prompts Phase-aware prompts based on the selected project stage, latest messages, open actions and available project records.
- intake: “Summarise the client’s brief from this chat.”
- scoping: “List feasibility risks before we proceed.”
- coordination: “What design decisions are still unresolved?”
- compliance: “What municipal submission items are missing?”
- delivery: “What site issues could affect time or cost?”
- closeout: “List documents still required for handover.”
AI ORCHESTRATION REQUIREMENTS AI should not replace professional approval. It should classify, suggest, summarise and route.
- classify incoming messages by phase, capture type and urgency.
- suggest conversions: action, RFI, instruction, approval, site log, council item, tender clarification, closeout item.
- summarise the project communication history by phase.
- extract next actions and responsible people.
- flag compliance and contractual risk language.
- prepare draft formal outputs, but require human approval before issue.
1. One communication record appears on mobile and desktop.
3. Files are uploaded through the existing Architex file storage approach, preferably Vercel Blob.
4. Firestore realtime subscriptions remain the source of truth for live chat.
5. The ProjectStage model controls phase-aware UI behaviour.
6. The delivery/construction phase retains site-heavy functionality.
7. AI tab has a visible “Suggested prompts” section.
8. Desktop view is a project message centre, not a duplicate standalone desktop chat app.
9. Mobile applet can run as part of the PWA and later be made installable/add-to-home-screen.
10. No AI-generated output is treated as issued/approved unless a human confirms it.
IMPLEMENTATION SLICES Slice 1 — Model and configuration
- Keep backward compatibility with jobId-based messages.
- Add phase-aware capture tools, AI suggested prompts and next actions.
- Add split-pane conversation + structured record/action panel.
- Add endpoint/service to classify messages and suggest conversions.
- Route outputs to existing services where possible.
- Create record links to submissions, tender packages, site logs, RFIs, invoices and closeout records.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE FOR GREG/AMY This should not be bolted on as an isolated demo app. It should become the next-generation replacement/extension of the existing src/components/Chat.tsx and src/services/messagingService.ts, preserving existing behaviour but adding phase, project, capture, action, file and AI metadata.

- Helps a client understand likely professional and statutory costs before appointing a team.

## 13. Architex platform transaction fee and escrow monetisation

Architex monetises project cash flow by charging a transparent platform transaction/service fee of approximately 1% on transactions processed through the platform. This must be disclosed in proposals, invoices, escrow funding requests, payment confirmations and ledger records.
- Total Architex service cost: 1.00% of the chargeable transaction base
- Client / payer contribution: 0.50% added on top of the professional fee or construction bill
- Professional / contractor / payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the amount released to the payee
- Architex receives both halves through the escrow/payment gateway flow
Example on a R100,000 professional fee or construction bill, excluding VAT and excluding statutory disbursements unless deliberately included:
- Client-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
- Client funds into escrow before VAT/payment-gateway effects: R100,500.00
- Payee-side Architex service fee at 0.50%: R500.00
Every proposal and bill generated through Architex must include a visible line item such as:

"Architex platform transaction/service fee: 1.00% total, shared equally between payer and payee. Client contribution: 0.50% added to this payment. Payee contribution: 0.50% deducted from the release amount. Processed through Architex escrow/payment gateway."
- Fee/bill before Architex transaction service fee
- VAT treatment and payment-gateway fees separately, pending tax/accounting confirmation
- Contractor construction bills / certified payment amounts
- Supplier bills where paid through Architex marketplace/escrow
- Payment gateway processing fees if separately charged
For each accepted proposal/payment stage, Architex should create a split settlement schedule:
1. Client funds gross amount into escrow: chargeableBase + clientPlatformFee + other included charges
2. Escrow records the full held amount
3. On milestone release, Architex deducts payeePlatformFee from payee gross release
5. Architex platform account receives clientPlatformFee + payeePlatformFee
6. Ledger records separate entries for escrow deposit, client platform fee, payee platform fee, payee release, refunds/reversals and gateway fees

- `src/services/financialLedgerService.ts` already records ledger entries and recognises `platform_fee`. It should be extended to distinguish `platform_fee_client_share` and `platform_fee_payee_share`.

- `src/services/paymentService.ts` already contains PayFast/escrow logic and currently defines `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENTAGE = 0.05`.
- `src/services/financialLedgerService.ts` already records ledger entries and recognises `platform_fee`.

- `src/types.ts` already contains `Payment`, `Escrow`, `EscrowV2`, `Invoice`, `LedgerEntry`, `ProjectStage`, `TenderPackage`, `Bid`, and role types for clients, BEPs, contractors, subcontractors and suppliers.
The code in this folder is intentionally framework-light and pure TypeScript so Greg/Amy can integrate it into the app without fighting UI dependencies.
Recommended integration paths in the Architex repo:
- Total Architex platform service fee: 1.00% of chargeable transaction base
- Client/payer share: 0.50% added to the amount paid into escrow
- Professional/contractor/supplier payee share: 0.50% deducted from the amount released
- Both shares are visible line items and settled to Architex through escrow/payment gateway
The platform fee is not hidden. Proposal, invoice, escrow funding screen and release statement must show the split clearly.
